vaping = inhaling vapour from an electronic cigarette
gambling addiction = an inability to control betting despite serious harm
rehab clinic = a centre that treats people for addiction, often with therapy and medical support
addictive substance = a drug or chemical that can create dependence
healthy lifestyle = habits such as balanced eating, activity, sleep and avoiding harmful substances
sedentary lifestyle = a way of living with little physical movement
childhood obesity = a level of body fat in children that is high enough to harm present and future health
undernutrition = poor health caused by too little food, or food that lacks essential nutrients
sleep deprivation = a lasting lack of enough sleep
mindfulness = paying attention to the present moment, often used to reduce stress
physical inactivity = not doing enough movement to protect health
disability = a physical, sensory, intellectual or mental condition that makes some activities harder
accessibility = how easily people with disabilities can use a place, service or product
reasonable adjustment = a practical change an employer or school must make so a disabled person can take part
wheelchair access = the possibility for a wheelchair user to enter and move around a place
sign language = a visual language using hands, face and body, used by many deaf people
visually impaired = having little or no sight
hearing impairment = partial or complete loss of hearing
learning disability = a reduced ability to understand new or complex information and to learn new skills
neurodiversity = the idea that brains differ and that autism, ADHD and similar conditions are variations, not only defects
